title: Sev2: 'Orion' customer GPU OOM cascade due to KV cache fragmentation — runtime salvage & patch
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Summary: On 2026-03-05 we observed a production-wide burst of GPU OOM failures affecting both Hosted and Dedicated pools for the Orion tenant (multi-service customer). Root cause analysis points to progressive KV cache fragmentation with leaked tombstones and uneven slab utilization which triggered kernel allocation spikes and eventual GPU OOM cascades under medium-length chat workloads. The incident manifested as increased tail latency, 5xx generator errors, and tenant isolation escalations.

Impact: ~12% of Orion requests returned OOM/failure over the incident window; three Dedicated nodes entered degraded mode and we had to temporarily drain and reprovision two nodes. Customer escalated to SEV2 and requested immediate mitigation and long-term fix.

Timeline (high level):
- 2026-03-05 09:12 UTC: Alerts from SLO monitors and customer Slack report.
- 2026-03-05 09:20 UTC: First mitigation applied — increased eviction aggressiveness for Orion pool and enabled per-tenant prefix eviction. Immediate drop in OOM rate but latency remained high.
- 2026-03-05 11:00 UTC: Hotpatch (runtime v2.3.1-hot1) deployed to Hosted pool: tombstone coalescer enabled + conservative allocator fallback. OOMs reduced by 85% for hosted.
- 2026-03-06 02:30 UTC: Dedicated nodes required a runtime binary rebuild to include new slab compaction hook; staged canary with 5% traffic.
- 2026-03-07 14:45 UTC: Canary passed real workload tests; rollout scheduled.

Root cause detail: The allocator's per-slab free list failed to coalesce freed KV entries when concurrent session handoffs occurred during a specific request mix (moderate sequence lengths with many short-lived sessions). This produced stranded tombstones and an imbalance in slab occupancy across CUDA arenas. On higher-concurrency hosts this forced large allocations to fall back to slow paths which triggered GPU page pressure and then OOM. Regression appears correlated with allocator refactor in runtime-2.2.0 that changed free-list handoff ordering.

Mitigations applied:
- Short term: Tuned eviction thresholds for Orion tenant; enabled aggressive KV TTL enforcement; temporarily increased Dedicated pool reservation for Orion.
- Hotfix: runtime v2.3.1-hot1 toggles tombstone coalescer and adds an allocator fence to prevent double-free races in session handoff. Deployed to Hosted within 2 hours; mitigated majority of OOMs.
- Runtime fix: PR introduces a compaction hook that periodically rescues stranded tombstones and rebalances slab occupancy across arenas, plus a KV index reconciliation pass during low-traffic windows. This is targeting runtime-2.3.2.

Rollout plan: Canary for runtime-2.3.2 on 5% Dedicated nodes for 24 hours with auto-rollback on any rise in OOMs or token-tail latency. Followed by 25% after 12h then full rollout if stable. Observability: new metrics added (kvcache.tombstone_count, allocator.fragmentation_ratio, slab.rebalance_ops) and dashboards updated: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/orion-ooms and linked alerts.

Post-incident follow-ups:
- Complete allocator handoff audit and add deterministic unit tests for handoff ordering (owner: Ravi).
- Add automated canary traffic generator for medium sequence-length workloads (owner: SRE).
- Customer postmortem and SLA credit proposal drafted (owner: CS).

Verify kvcache.tombstone_count decreases by >90% compared to pre-hotfix baseline
Confirm allocator.fragmentation_ratio stays below 0.20 under 95th percentile load
Run golden prompt regression suite and ensure no deltas in generation quality
postmortem_actions: Add deterministic allocator handoff unit tests (owner: Ravi)
Add monthly slab rebalance job to prevent tombstone buildup (owner: SRE)
Integrate kvcache fragmentation alerts into default tenant SLOs (owner: Observability)
Provide remediation timeline and SLA credit to Orion via CS (owner: Customer Success)
